LordSDay.title: LordSDay
LordSDay.description: Represents one of the 52 Lord's Days in the Heidelberg Catechism.

id.description: Unique identifier for the LordSDay entity.

dayNumber.description: The sequential number of the Lord's Day (1-52).

titleTelugu.description: The title of the Lord's Day in Telugu.

CatechismQuestionAnswer.title: CatechismQuestionAnswer
CatechismQuestionAnswer.description: Represents a single question and its corresponding answer from the Heidelberg Catechism.

id.description: Unique identifier for the CatechismQuestionAnswer entity.

lordSDayId.description: Reference to the LordSDay this question and answer pair belongs to. (Relationship: LordSDay 1:N CatechismQuestionAnswer)

questionNumber.description: The global sequential number of the question within the entire catechism (e.g., 1 to 129). This also implies order within a Lord's Day.

questionTextTelugu.description: The full text of the question in Telugu.

answerTextTelugu.description: The full text of the answer in Telugu.

definition.description: Top-level collection for each 'Lord's Day' of the Heidelberg Catechism. Each document represents a single Lord's Day and contains its number and Telugu title. Documents in this collection are publicly readable.

params.name: lordSDayId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific Lord's Day.

definition.description: Subcollection under each 'Lord's Day' containing the questions and answers for that day. Each document represents a single question and answer pair, including its global question number, Telugu question text, and Telugu answer text. It also includes the 'lordSDayId' as a denormalized reference to its parent Lord's Day, providing a direct link within the document. Documents in this subcollection are publicly readable.

params.name: lordSDayId
params.description: The unique identifier for the parent Lord's Day.

params.name: qaId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific Catechism Question and Answer pair.

firestore.reasoning:
The recommended Firestore structure is designed for a static, read-only application, prioritizing simplicity, efficient data retrieval, and explicit hierarchy. The core content (Lord's Days and Catechism Questions/Answers) is publicly accessible, meaning authorization rules are straightforward, and complex denormalization for authorization is not required.

**Authorization Independence:** In this specific context, where all content is publicly readable and static, the concept of 'Authorization Independence' primarily translates to ensuring that security rules do not rely on `get()` calls for parent documents to determine access. Since all data will be `allow read: if true;`, there are no hierarchical authorization dependencies to manage. If, in the future, administrative write access were introduced, an `/admin_users/{uid}` collection would be used for DBAC (Database Access Control) to allow writes, keeping write authorization independent of the content's structure.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):** This structure naturally supports Query-Able Paths (QAPs). 
1.  The `/lords_days` collection allows for efficient listing of all 'Lord's Day' titles (for the 'Lord's Day List View'). Security rules will simply allow all reads (`match /lords_days/{lordSDayId} { allow read: if true; }`).
2.  The `/lords_days/{lordSDayId}/catechism_qas` subcollection allows for efficient retrieval of all questions and answers for a specific 'Lord's Day' (for the 'Catechism Detail View'). Security rules will similarly allow all reads (`match /lords_days/{lordSDayId}/catechism_qas/{qaId} { allow read: if true; }`).

**Structural Segregation & Access Modeling:** All data shares the same security posture (public read-only), so there's no need to segregate public from private data. The structure uses hierarchical paths (`/lords_days/{lordSDayId}/catechism_qas/{qaId}`) to represent the natural parent-child relationship between a 'Lord's Day' and its corresponding questions and answers. This makes the data intuitive to navigate and query. The `lordSDayId` field is included in the `CatechismQuestionAnswer` document, as per the schema, even though its parent's ID is implicit in the path. This serves as a strong foreign key reference within the document itself, potentially aiding in data integrity or cross-collection queries if the `catechism_qas` ever needed to be queried independently of its parent path in a different context (though not strictly necessary for this app's current requirements).
